message.content:
CONTRADICTED

1. Density: Paper claims Q‑Tersoff density error ≈0% and ML‑Tersoff ≈9.2% at 300 K. Your replication finds:
   - Q‑Tersoff: 1.735 g/cm³ (VERBATIM) and 2.029 g/cm³ (NPT), i.e. 34.5% and 23.4% errors vs 2.648 g/cm³.
   - ML‑Tersoff: 1.591 g/cm³ (VERBATIM) and 1.856 g/cm³ (NPT), i.e. 39.9% and 29.9% errors.
   These are off by ~20–35 percentage points from the published errors and never approach the claimed 0% / 9.2%.

2. Structure at 0 K: Paper treats quartz as preserved; your minimizations give:
   - Q‑Tersoff: ρ=2.100 (20.7% error), Si–O–Si=168.78° (≈+25°), O–Si–O=111.79° (≈+2.3°).
   - ML‑Tersoff: ρ=1.949 (26.4% error), Si–O–Si=174.99° (≈+31°), O–Si–O=111.80° (≈+2.3°).
   The hexagonal cell distorts (c dilates ≈50%), indicating a non‑quartz minimum, contradicting the implied “alpha‑quartz” state.

3. Angles at 298 K NPT:
   - Q‑Tersoff: Si–O–Si=147.55° vs 143.7° (error +3.85°; paper: 1.7°), O–Si–O=108.22° vs 109.47° (error −1.25°; paper: 0.3°).
     Both errors are 2–4× larger than reported.
   - ML‑Tersoff: Si–O–Si=128.68° vs 143.7° (error −15.02°; paper: +7°), wrong sign and ≈2× the claimed magnitude; O–Si–O=105.95° (error −3.52° vs claimed 0.4°).

4. Coordination: Paper implicitly assumes a tetrahedral network; your NPT results show:
   - Q‑Tersoff: ≈97.6% 4‑fold Si.
   - ML‑Tersoff: only ≈77% 4‑fold Si (≈23% broken tetrahedra).
   This contradicts the implied preservation of proper SiO₄ tetrahedral coordination for ML‑Tersoff.

5. Across all tested protocols using the released potentials and seed, key quantitative claims for alpha‑quartz (density, angles, and coordination) do not match, with specific discrepancies in the 20–40% range for density and up to ≈31° for Si–O–Si.
